purpose: release/derive.rs (the path release plan/release execute actually run) is missing checks that commands/publish.rs::plan_publish (preview-only) already has, and diverges from it in cycle handling, registry validation, npm access defaulting, release notes, and package selection. This spec makes release/derive.rs a strict behavioral superset of plan_publish for these cases.
scope: release/derive.rs's publish-plan derivation; release_decision.rs's derive_selected_release_decision and ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason; crate::toposort's shared dev-cycle edge filter; commands/release/binding.rs::prepared_registry_binding and registry_endpoint.rs::canonical_registry_url as the single registry-trust validator; registry_argv.rs's npm default-access helper; ForgeReleaseOperation.notes derivation and fallback; PublishTarget::is_implemented() enforcement in plan derivation.
non_goals: CLI command naming, --help text, hidden-vs-shown subcommand list (SPEC-DX-RELEASE-CLI family).
CI pre-flight exit-code and default-feature coverage (SPEC-DX-CORRECTNESS-CI).

Whether a package's current version needs releasing (ReleaseInclusionReason::UnreleasedVersion) -- owned by SPEC-DX-RELEASE-COMMAND; this spec only requires derive.rs not to add or drop packages from that selection.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: [UPDATED 2026-09-24] Given a selected package with a runtime, optional, or peer workspace dependency edge to a standalone unreleased workspace package that is absent from the release decision, release/derive.rs's plan derivation fails with GraphError::ReleaseSelectionInvalid{reason: ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::DependencyNotSelected} -- a generalized variant covering any unreleased runtime/optional/peer workspace dependency (not scoped to Platform-manifest dependencies specifically), added in callisto-graph/src/error.rs (crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs:740-741; crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:542-585,1093), not commands/publish.rs::plan_publish's separate MissingPlatformDependency error.

Given the same dependency shape as AC-1 but the platform package's current version is already released (has a matching tag), release/derive.rs's plan derivation succeeds without requiring the platform package to be separately selected.

Given a dependency graph where two packages form a cycle only through dev-dependency edges, release/derive.rs's DAG build succeeds and orders them, instead of failing with a cycle error -- using callisto-graph/src/toposort.rs::toposort_with_edge_filter with the same dev-dependency edge filter that commands/publish.rs::publish_order uses.

Given a graph containing a mixed cycle where one edge is a runtime dependency and another is dev-only, release/derive.rs's DAG build (via toposort_with_edge_filter) still fails with a cycle error -- only the dev-only edge is excluded from cycle detection, not the runtime edge.

Given an npm package whose package.json publishConfig.registry is an https URL that does not exactly match a url on an npm-kind entry in callisto.toml's [registries] table, release/derive.rs's plan derivation rejects it with GraphError::UntrustedNpmRegistry via commands/release/binding.rs::prepared_registry_binding -- the single shared validator both release/derive.rs and commands/publish.rs call, after publish.rs's own duplicate inline check is deleted.

Given an npm package whose publishConfig.registry is a non-https URL (e.g. http://), prepared_registry_binding rejects it via registry_endpoint.rs::canonical_registry_url's scheme check with GraphError::UnsafeRegistryBinding, checked before host matching, even if the host would otherwise be approved; a matching-host but non-https override is never reachable as UntrustedNpmRegistry.

Given a scoped (@scope/name) npm package configured to publish with no explicit --access flag and no publishConfig.access set, release/derive.rs's derived plan defaults that package's PublishTarget::Npm access to public, using a shared npm_default_access(name, explicit) -> Option<NpmAccess> helper in registry_argv.rs that both release/derive.rs and commands/registry_argv.rs::npm_publish_flags call for the same input; the defaulted access value is part of the operation's target_fingerprint. The same default applies when the package is dispatched as a PlatformPublish prerequisite (AC-1b).

For a GitHub forge release, release/derive.rs's plan derivation sets a new ForgeReleaseOperation.notes: ReleaseNotes field (ReleaseNotes::Section(String) | ReleaseNotes::Generated{reason: NotesFallback}) in commands/release/provider/mod.rs, computed via a shared changelog-notes function performing the same CHANGELOG.md section extraction as commands/publish.rs::resolve_changelog_section; the release effect passes --notes-file when notes is Section and falls back to gh release's --generate-notes when notes is Generated. notes is derived text and is excluded from the release intent digest -- it does not affect rerun/adoption identity.

Given a package with a configured changelog path where the file is missing, has no matching version heading, or the matched section is empty, release/derive.rs's plan derivation sets notes to ReleaseNotes::Generated{reason} with reason one of NotesFallback::FileMissing, ::SectionMissing, or ::SectionEmpty respectively, rather than failing the plan; the release effect falls back to gh release's --generate-notes and prints `notes: using generated notes (<reason>)` to stderr naming the package.

Given an unreadable (not merely missing) changelog file, release/derive.rs's plan derivation sets notes to ReleaseNotes::Generated{reason: NotesFallback::Unreadable} rather than aborting the plan; the release effect falls back to --generate-notes and prints the same stderr notice pattern as AC-8 with a reason distinguishing this read-failure case.

release_decision.rs::derive_selected_release_decision accepts package selectors as exact ecosystem/name strings only (no bare-name or prefix matching); a name that resolves in the workspace but does not appear in the derived plan fails with GraphError::ReleaseSelectionInvalid{reason: ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::NotARelease} when the package is not a release candidate at all, or ::NoDispatchableTarget when it is a release candidate but has nothing to dispatch -- replacing the current single NotInPlan variant with this two-way distinction, matching commands/publish.rs's existing NotInPlanReason split.

Given a package configured with a PublishTarget where PublishTarget::is_implemented() returns false, release/derive.rs's plan derivation fails with GraphError::PublishTargetNotImplemented{package, target} and produces no plan -- it does not degrade to a Warning diagnostic and skip that target.

Given a fixed set of packages selected by release_decision.rs's ReleaseInclusionReason::UnreleasedVersion check, release/derive.rs's plan derivation produces exactly one plan entry per selected package (excluding platform prerequisites folded per AC-1/AC-1b) -- it never adds a package absent from that selection or silently drops a selected package from the derived plan.

Re-running release execute over an already-published release, where every selected operation's target state already matches (e.g. the tag and registry version already exist), resolves each operation's preflight to AlreadySatisfied and re-dispatches none of them; the receipt records AlreadySatisfied for every operation in the plan, not only a subset.

reasoning: Grounded against origin/fix/release-run-simplify@9be31095: ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason (error.rs:678-685) confirmed to currently have only {Duplicate, NotInPlan, DuplicateRegistryTarget} -- PlatformDependencyNotSelected, NotARelease, NoDispatchableTarget are new variants. ForgeReleaseOperation (provider/mod.rs:66-70) confirmed to have only {tag, prerelease}, no notes field. prepared_registry_binding (binding.rs:42) and canonical_registry_url (registry_endpoint.rs:63) confirmed as the existing single-validator target, with canonical_registry_url's scheme check running before host-match. crate::toposort (toposort.rs: toposort_impl, toposort_with_edge_filter) confirmed to exist as the natural shared-filter target. registry_argv.rs's npm_publish_flags/npm_publish_argv confirmed to exist with inline access handling but no npm_default_access helper -- this spec adds it. PublishTarget::is_implemented (ecosystem.rs:197) and Ecosystem::is_implemented (ecosystem.rs:81, matches Cargo|Npm|Pypi) confirmed to exist already; AC-11 requires derive.rs to consult it and fail hard rather than degrade. Added AC-1b to make the release-already-published exemption in AC-1's rationale testable rather than left implicit.
revision_note: 2026-09-24 drift pass: AC-1 rewritten -- the code uses a generalized DependencyNotSelected variant (any unreleased runtime/optional/peer workspace dependency), not a Platform-specific PlatformDependencyNotSelected variant.
